name: Motorcycle
description: Any motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels, including motor scooters: the default category for an electric two- or three-wheeler that is neither an electric-assisted bicycle nor a motorized bicycle. Defined by Minnesota Statutes §169.011, subd. 44; a 2026 bill (HF 3785 / SF 4186) to define e-motos as electric motorcycles didn't pass.
restrictions: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels on the ground; motor scooters are motorcycles
An electric two- or three-wheeler faster than 30 mph or more powerful than 2 brake horsepower (1,492 W) is too much for a motorized bicycle and lands here
No limit on motor power or speed
Needs a title, and a title needs a 17-digit VIN, which a machine lacking federal motor vehicle safety equipment can't get; without a title and registration it can't be ridden on public roads
Riders need a driver's license with a two-wheeled vehicle (motorcycle) endorsement
Riders and passengers under 18, and anyone riding on an instruction permit, must wear a helmet; every rider must wear eye protection
Registered with a rear license plate, and must carry liability insurance
May pass between lanes of traffic only at 25 mph or less and no more than 15 mph faster than traffic, and never in school zones or single-lane work zones
